items.title: Sal Gutierrez Interview, 1970-01-15
items.q: Interviewer mentions Gordon Kirst was in the band and played piano; Interviewee does not mention Gordon Kirst, only discusses Steve and Armand Hug.

ctx.x: Why don't you find some of those old records and show Dick's hair? By the back and so on. Your uncle went away, Jules, went away with Tom Brown? I think that's when he left around 1918, when my sister was born, my third sister. And I remember I was little, I was about four, I guess. And I remember he came to the house to say goodbye. And he never did come back. I mean, he came here in 65 in the hurricane. And he played on the guitar for us. That ain't good.

Yeah, he told me that. You're on the fourth rail now. Heavens to Betsy. Yeah, I didn't know. You were telling me about Gordon Kirst before we forget it. He had the band. Yeah, yeah, see the fart there, they got help that the IJ Kirst couldn't play nothing. And Gordon was in the band, see, piano player. So they put Gordon with the baton leading the band.

So naturally, Steve got to play. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. So naturally, Steve got on me in the band to play piano. They all hung up to play piano in the band, not the Blue Room, see. I was the first band in the Blue Room, before I started going to name bands, you know, name bands. The same thing happened at the Club Forest when they had the bands out there, Juice Bidoux and Lou Yandies and bands and bands and bands and they…
